newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE WATCHES SKIES FOR CLUES ON NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE WATCHES SKIES FOR CLUES ON NEXT WEEK.

text.p: The Polish bourse's performance next week is seen largely dependent on flood-water levels as investors watch the sky this weekend to see if an expected wave of heavy rain causes a second round of flooding.
Heavy rains already fell on Western Poland on Friday morning, including areas already hit by flooding, but not all weather forecasters were pessimistic.
Floods in the past two weeks have left suspnded trade in four listed firms -- Polifarb Wroclaw , Rafako, ZEW and Viscoplast.

"The flooding has an unclear effect on the macroeconomy, whether we're talking about the first or second (possible) wave and doesn't encourage investment decisions....It seems players are at least holding back," said Bogdan Duszek of PKO BP house.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 3.1 percent this week to 15,348.9 points.
Analysts said it was not year clear to what degree Poland's planned 2.8-percent 1997 budget deficit target might be affected by flood-relief aid.

They said another negative sign was the central bank head's statement on Thursday that official interest rates could rise to help offset monetary effects of the bank's 2.5-billion-zloty emergency credit line for the government.

But analysts said a good sign was Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz's comments that she saw no substantial risk of a significant zloty depreciation after many investors trimmed their Polish T-bill portfolios causing recent zloty volatility.

"Many foreign investors have already left the fixed-income market and maybe will start thinking about accumulating shares of firms that gain from flood reconstruction," said Robert Nejman, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.
Analysts said such firms included construction, furniture and food companies, such as several of the Mostostal builders which saw significant gains towards week's end.
Analysts said flood concerns could take investor attention away from June financial results, most due on Friday.
They also said the run-up to the September 21 parliamentary elections would limit the market's upside in coming weeks.
